_comment: Pages read on 2026-10-21 for the true-credits batch: one record per citation read. passage and note: the passage id and the 0-based index of the note in its layers list in config/layers.json; kind: the note's kind; source, on and at: the citation as config/layers.json gives it; url: the page the citation links to, fetched on the date and at the UTC time given, with the final URL, the HTTP status and the SHA-256 of the body received.

status: "confirmed" (already cited, read again and found to state the point) or "added" (cited from this batch, as a further writer where a note lost one or where counting writers by person showed fewer than its label claims; read_for says which). left out: the reading behind a removal.

quote: the writer's words as found on the page, only for public-domain writers; '...' joins parts that appear in that order on the page, and a bracketed verse such as [Genesis 32:31] marks a part under a neighbouring heading. Spelling and misprints are the page's own. pointer: for the NET Bible notes and for the Pulpit Commentary (Bible Hub's digital text says "Copyright (c) 2001, 2003, 2005, 2006, 2010 by BibleSoft, inc."), where on the page the point is made, never its words.

verdict (founder's decision 20, 2026-10-21): whether the cited comment respects or denies Scripture, judged on its own words by the test of the spec's section 4.2 (an event Scripture reports as history called fiction or legend; a book or passage given to another writer or time than Scripture names; Scripture said to err; a book's place in Scripture questioned). Reporting another man's view in order to answer it is not a denial. The authorship, canon, error and myth word lists of the Voices build were run over each comment (and over the book's introduction when the link opens a chapter 1 page) to find what to read closely; decided says what they turned up. scripture_check names the group of spec section 4.4 a reading belongs to.

fetched_again: the page fetched a second time later the same day, with its UTC time, HTTP status and SHA-256, and words_found: whether the record's quoted words were found again on it (null for a record that gives a pointer instead of words). Done for every "denies" reading, for the introduction behind A. S. Aglen's removal and for 1 in 5 of the "respects" readings. It confirms the words are there; each verdict was reached once, by reading.

left_out records what decision 20 removed: A. S. Aglen's 12 citations (his introduction to Jonah, read again on this date, with its words) and one passage of F. W. Farrar's; set_aside lists passages set aside for want of a writer (none). A record above whose citation has since been removed matches no live citation, and the build counts it as such.

Whether history or parable, it conveys in the most striking way some of the profoundest truths of religion

But the figure is none the less striking, the character none the less instructive, if it is the creation of fiction; and the incident, even if unhistorical, carries a wealth of profound spiritual truth.
